name: Question 20
problem:
A laptop's battery life on a single charge is normally distributed with an average of $8$ hours and an unknown standard deviation. Tests show that $20%$ of laptops die after $11$ hours of usage. Assuming a normal model, what percentage of laptops will last less than $6$ hours on a single charge? **Round the answer to $1$ decimal place.**

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $\,p\,$ | $0.75$ | $0.8$ | $0.85$ | $0.9$ | $0.95$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,0.6745\,$ | $\,0.8416\,$ | $\,1.0364\,$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ |

*In addition, you're given the following table of values for $p=Φ(z).$*

| $z$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.7\,$ | $\,0.2236\,$ | $\,0.2206\,$ | $\,0.2177\,$ |
| $\,-0.6\,$ | $\,0.2546\,$ | $\,0.2514\,$ | $\,0.2483\,$ |
| $\,-0.5\,$ | $\,0.2877\,$ | $\,0.2843\,$ | $\,0.2810\,$ |

Approximately
{{field-1}}$%$ of laptops will last less than $6$ hours on a single charge.
worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the number of hours of a laptop's battery life. Then we have $X∼N(8,{\sigma }^{2}),$ and we want to find $P(X<6).$ But first, we need to find the standard deviation $\sigma .$ 

We know that $P(X>11)=0.20.$ First, we convert this to a cumulative probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 11) & =1-P(X>11) \\  & =1-0.20 \\  & =0.80\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 11) & =0.80 \\ P(Z\le \frac{11-8}{\sigma }) & =0.80 \\ Φ(\frac{3}{\sigma }) & =0.80 \\ \frac{3}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.80)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.80)=0.8416.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sigma } & =0.8416 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{3}{0.8416} \\ \sigma  & ≈3.5646.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can solve for $P(X\le 6)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 6) & =P(Z\le \frac{6-8}{3.5646}) \\  & ≈P(Z\le -0.56) \\  & =Φ(-0.56) \\  & =0.2877 \\  & ≈28.8%\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, approximately $28.8%$ of laptops will last less than $6$ hours on a single charge.
